entries.mechanism:
South Carolina's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP state option;
PolicyEngine models gross screen x1.3 FPL, x2.0 for elderly/disabled
households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in
the composed us-sc/snap/fy-2026 program, which applies only the standard
federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
persisted output surface: household gross income sits inside the band
above the federal 130 percent limit the composed program applies and at
or below the state's BBCE screen, verified against axiom's own computed
gross income and limit. Axiom-side modeling boundary, tracked for
encoding in rulespec-us#1098. Requested-month selector audit retained 20 of 20 rows; vanished cases: none; materially moved rows: 0.

Reverified on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The exact-household signature and explicit K-12 counterfactual reproduce the mechanism: PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7). The sole minor is a valid household under 273.1(a)(1), but wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so Axiom correctly fails the income gate and returns zero benefit. Requested-month selector audit retained 2 of 2 rows; vanished cases: none; materially moved rows: 2 (ecps-29280 right 299.66998291015625 -> 298.0; ecps-29677 right 299.66998291015625 -> 298.0).

households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in

federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
